# swarmops serve

Serve the stores under --root to stock git: fetch, clone and push over ssh as a forced command, or over smart HTTP as a CGI program. One process per connection, no daemon.

Over ssh, an authorized\_keys line runs it: command="swarmops serve --root /srv/so --as person/ada",restrict ssh-ed25519 .... The client's git-upload-pack '&lt;store&gt;.git' or git-receive-pack '&lt;store&gt;.git' (SSH\_ORIGINAL\_COMMAND) names a store by its directory under --root. With --cgi, a web server runs it for smart HTTP, its PATH\_INFO starting with the store's name; TLS and authentication are the web server's.

The caller is named by --as alone, or with --cgi by --user-family &lt;family&gt; as &lt;family&gt;/$REMOTE\_USER: the global --as default, $SWARMOPS\_AGENT, does not apply to serve, nor does $SWARMOPS\_RUN\_ID, so that the serving account's environment names no caller. A connection that names none is refused with E\_AUTH (details.reason no\_identity), whatever it asks for. The store's access.toml grants read, push, force and land; a caller it names but does not grant is refused with E\_POLICY\_DENIED.

The branches are served as refs/heads/&lt;name&gt;, main among them, and the tags as refs/tags/&lt;path&gt;. A push moves a store ref by compare-and-swap: main only forward along first parents. A push to refs/land/&lt;target&gt; lands its commits onto &lt;target&gt; as swarmops land does, and reports a conflict on git's remote: lines.

A refusal before git starts prints one ERR pkt-line on stdout, which git shows as remote error: &lt;CODE&gt;: &lt;message&gt;, and the envelope on stderr; with --cgi, a Status: header and the same text. --hook proc-receive is the entry git runs inside a push, from the hook file serve writes; it takes no --as. --stdio, the store-to-store sync, is not served yet.

## Syntax

```text
swarmops serve [OPTIONS]
```

## Required arguments

None.

## Optional arguments

The command also takes the [global options](../cli.md#global-options).

### `--root`

Syntax: `--root <DIR>`.

The directory whose subdirectories are the stores served, each by its name.

### `--cgi`

Syntax: `--cgi`.

Serve one CGI request: smart HTTP behind a web server.

### `--user-family`

Syntax: `--user-family <FAMILY>`.

With --cgi: name the caller &lt;FAMILY&gt;/$REMOTE\_USER, the user the web server authenticated.

### `--hook`

Syntax: `--hook <HOOK>`.

Run as the hook git runs inside a push: proc-receive, from the hook file serve writes. Values: `proc-receive`: git's `proc-receive`: it decides each command of a push.

### `--stdio`

Syntax: `--stdio`.

Serve the store-to-store sync on stdin and stdout: not served yet.

## Examples

### CLI

No recorded example yet.

## Return information

`swarmops serve` prints no envelope on stdout, which carries git's protocol: a refusal before git starts is one `ERR` pkt-line there (with `--cgi`, a `Status:` header and its text), and the envelope goes to stderr, as for a command line it refuses.

Envelope `op`: `serve`.

Exit codes:

- `0`: Success.

## Errors

No golden step shows this command failing yet.

Any command that opens a store may also fail with a store error, such as [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo), [`E_IO`](../errors.md#e_io) or [`E_STORE_CORRUPT`](../errors.md#e_store_corrupt); a command line the grammar refuses is [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg) (exit 2).
